Situation1: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Situation2: A main production unit has paused for thirty minutes because of recurring sensor errors.
Story: My phone buzzed with a sharp message from Sam, my closest friend. He thought I was annoyed with him, all because my last text was too blunt. I could hear the hurt in his reply, and I knew I had to call him right away, explain, and clear things up before the misunderstanding grew. But at that exact moment, my supervisor’s voice crackled through the radio: the main production unit was down again, sensor errors halting everything for half an hour now. I was the only one on shift who could diagnose the issue quickly. The pressure was on—every minute the line was down cost the company money, and everyone expected me to fix it, fast. My phone felt heavy in my hand. I could picture Sam waiting for my call, needing reassurance, while the production team waited for me to get the machines running. My mind raced, torn between the urgent beep of the factory and the silent ache of my friend’s message, both demanding my attention, both impossible to ignore.
